extracted.intended_audience: beginners who want to learn to solder, educators who want to teach soldering, makers/translators who want to reuse or translate the comic
extracted.subtask_description: Announcing and distributing the seven-page 'Soldering is Easy' comic book: how to use it to teach beginners, what source/formats are available for printing or translating, and how translators can contribute and be credited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target learner scope / learning outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: This seven page comic book explains in detail and with pictures how to make a good solder connection and teaches all the other bits and pieces of knowledge needed to successfully solder together an electronic kit, even if you’ve never soldered before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for absolute beginners; should include clear step-by-step pictures and explanations focused on producing a good solder connection and completing simple electronic kits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and permitted uses (Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comic is released under a Creative Commons license (Attribution-ShareAlike), so you are free to teach with it, color it, modify it, share it with your friends, translate it, and basically do whatever you like with it!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users must provide attribution and apply the same ShareAlike license to derivative works. The license explicitly permits teaching, coloring, modification, sharing, and translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation workflow and recommended source
rubrics_metrics.description: A PDF version without text and 300 DPI images without text are available for translation; the Comic Life source file (FullSolderComic.zip) is provided and is probably the best place to start if you are making a translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using the Comic Life source you will need a Mac and a copy of Comic Life. Translators should use no-text images or the source file to insert translated text cleanly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formats provided for distribution and reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple formats are provided: PDF, Amazon Kindle (.mobi), ePub, 11×17 booklet PDF (that can be folded into an actual comic), high-resolution 300 DPI images, and the Comic Life source file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick the format appropriate to your use: 11×17 booklet for printing/folding, .mobi/ePub for e-readers, 300 DPI images for high-quality prints or layout work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of no-text/print-ready assets for translators and reusers
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a PDF version without text and a ZIP of 300 DPI images without text specifically provided 'for translation'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these assets to produce translations that preserve original art; they lower risk of layout/quality loss compared to translating embedded text in a flattened PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to contribute a translation and receive linking/credit
rubrics_metrics.description: If you create a translation, please post a comment here and I’ll link to it! If you’re looking for help with a translation, you can try posting in the forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translators are expected to post a comment on the announcement to be linked and credited; forum posting is suggested for collaboration or help. The site lists translators' names and languages as credit examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and credit expectation for translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists translators by language (e.g., 'Arabic — Ahmed Mo’ni', 'Chinese — XinCheJian', etc.) and gives special thanks to contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contributing a translation, provide translator name and language so the maintainers can list and credit you. Example table on page shows how credits are displayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical printing/layout guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: An 11×17 version is available that you can fold into an actual comic book (with 8.5×11 pages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the booklet PDF for creating a physical comic; follow the intended page sizes to fold correctly into a booklet.
